summary: Re-ran the molecular tests for M1-S01 (object-model, agent metadata-builder) of build northwind-sales at scale project, after the N3-F-01 repair (reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 1; deploy-order.md section 6) removed <default>true</default> from the opening stage of both BusinessProcess files. Both always-on checks (xml over 8 files, manifest against package.xml) passed, and all three plan-declared checkers (check_opportunity_management.py, check_picklist_and_value_sets.py, check_object_creation_and_design.py) exited 0 against the post-repair artefacts, reproducing the exact messages their step-note fixtures predicted. check-outputs confirmed all 9 declared outputs present, non-empty and parseable, and their hashes were captured fresh into results.json.artefact_hashes. The two declared manual tests are deferred verbatim to the M1 milestone gate. Step moved built -> tested.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly (agents/step-tester/AGENT.md Step 7).

process_observations.observation: The repair was scoped exactly as deploy-order.md section 6 describes: only the opening-stage <values> block in each BusinessProcess file lost its <default>true</default> element (Qualify in Enterprise_Sales_Process, Renewal Review in Renewal_Sales_Process); the remaining five <values> blocks in each file still carry <default>false</default> unchanged, and the other seven declared outputs were untouched.

package.xml under artefacts/M1-S01/ still names exactly the 7 members the step's outputs produce post-repair, one <name> block per type, matching the manifest test's description verbatim -- the repair touched only <default> elements inside two already-manifested BusinessProcess files, so no manifest member or file was added or removed.

All three cited-skill checkers passed clean against the post-repair artefacts and reproduced the exact output strings recorded in the step's acceptance_tests[].description, so none of them were sensitive to the removed <default>true</default> element -- consistent with the finding being an org-side rejection (N3-F-01) rather than a locally-detectable defect.

None of this step's five cited skills document a per-BusinessProcess or per-RecordType default-stage mechanism for Opportunity; deploy-order.md section 6 records this gap as an inference ('UNVERIFIED (2026-09-18)') rather than a grounded claim, and it names a real open question -- which stage a new Enterprise or Renewal Opportunity actually opens on -- that no checker here can test and that the section 4 verification SOQL is the only way to close.

set-status printed a plan-wide WARN naming this step specifically: admin/sales-process-mapping (cited in M1-S01.skills[]) ships check_sales_process_mapping.py but no acceptance test on this step or on milestone M1 runs it. Per this agent's scope guardrails a missing declared test is reported, never invented, so it is not run here; whether the checker adds coverage this step's three declared checkers do not already provide is a call for whoever amends the step (--add-checker) or drops the citation, not for this run.

deploy-order.md section 0 still leads with the sf project retrieve start / merge instruction for StandardValueSet:OpportunityStage and states the deactivation risk in the same paragraph, and the literal string 'Commit' does not appear anywhere in OpportunityStage.standardValueSet-meta.xml -- both manual tests still read consistently with what they claim, though this agent does not tick them.

M1-S01 is tested again after its repair; the runs[] history shows it had already reached documented once before this repair reset it, so build-doc-keeper's prior workbook/traceability/decisions rows for this step now describe the pre-repair artefacts.
